evidence.name: CarCrashDamageProcessing

function_ir.summary: Advances the car crash damage animation. Early-returns unless the damage timer float at this+0xDC is positive and the damage data pointer at this+0x157C is non-null. On the first frame (timer equal to 0.01) it randomly picks an impact type and an impact origin (one of several screen-edge offsets written to this+0x1580/0x1584) using RandLCGRandomNumberGenerator, then zeroes cleanup fields this+0x18EC/0x18F0. Each call decrements the timer by FloatFieldAccessor (frame delta); when the timer expires the damage pointer and timer are cleared, otherwise the damage rects are rendered via sub_495DC0 with viewport data from InitViewportDimensions, SceneEntityCleanup runs on the argument, and ShortComputation_7250(1) is invoked. Returns 1 on a normal update.

local_names.this: car/vehicle crash-damage object whose damage state lives at +0x157C
local_names.a2: argument passed through to SceneEntityCleanup (identity not established here)
local_names.v3: damage data pointer read from this+0x157C
local_names.v4: int at v3+4, used as one screen-edge origin reference
local_names.v5: int at v3+12, used as one screen-edge origin reference
local_names.v6: RandLCGRandomNumberGenerator % 3 result for the type-1 impact path
local_names.v7: v6 - 1, selects between two type-1 sub-directions
local_names.v8: remaining damage timer after subtracting the frame delta
local_names.v10: overflow flag C0 from the timer subtraction
local_names.v11: overflow flag C3 from the timer subtraction

operations.description: Return 0 when the damage timer float at this+0xDC is not positive (<= 0.0); this is the lifetime gate of the animation.
Read the damage data pointer v3 from this+0x157C; return 0 when it is null.
v4 = *(v3 + 4) and v5 = *(v3 + 12); these two ints from the damage data struct act as screen-edge origin references for the direction pick.
First-frame path: when the DWORD at this+0xDC equals 1008981770 (float 0.01) the impact type and origin are randomized once.
If the impact type at this+0x1578 is zero, seed it with RandLCGRandomNumberGenerator % 2 so each damage instance picks one of two impact families.

Impact type 0: switch on RandLCGRandomNumberGenerator % 8 (dispatch via jump table global jpt_4960A2) writing eight distinct origin pairs to this+0x1580 (X) and this+0x1584 (Y), combining the 800/-800 X values and -600/600/v4/v5 Y values.

Impact type 1: switch on RandLCGRandomNumberGenerator % 3 (dispatch via jump table global jpt_4960C3) selecting three sub-directions; v6==1 writes 600 to this+0x1584, v6==2 writes 800 to this+0x1580, otherwise v5 is kept as X, and the fall-through sets this+0x1584 to -600 before jumping to the shared cleanup label.
Shared cleanup label reached by impact types 1/2/3/4: zero the DWORD at this+0x18F0 and the byte at this+0x18EC.
v8 = (float)this+0xDC - FloatFieldAccessor(this); write v8 back to this+0xDC, i.e. decrement the damage timer by the frame delta each call.
If the subtraction raised the overflow flags (v10 | v11), the timer expired: clear the damage data pointer this+0x157C and the timer this+0xDC to 0; otherwise run the render path.

Render path: compute v14 = v8 * 100.0 using the float constants read from flt_59E440/flt_59E6F8, obtain the viewport via InitViewportDimensions(this), then call sub_495DC0(this, viewport, v14) to draw the impact damage rectangles.
SceneEntityCleanup(a2) runs on the function's second argument as part of the per-frame update.
ShortComputation_7250(1) is invoked with constant 1 after the frame update.
Return 1 on the normal update path. Called by sub_496E90; the crash-damage display system drives this per-frame.

unresolved: Semantics of the two ints at v3+4 and v3+12 (screen-edge references) are inferred; their meaning inside the damage data struct is not proven.
Exact literal values stored at float globals flt_59E440 and flt_59E6F8 (presumed 100.0 and related scale constants) are not read from this packet.
Meaning of the cleanup fields this+0x18EC (byte) and this+0x18F0 (dword) is unknown.
Purpose of the impact type 0 vs type 1 families and why type 1 skips the shared direction table is not established.
Identity/role of SceneEntityCleanup's argument a2 is unresolved.
